title: Observability pulse: tracing sync and cost telemetry log - 2026-04-02
content:
Meeting: Observability team weekly deep-dive (tracing + dashboards + cost telemetry)
Date: 2026-04-02 09:30–10:30 PT
Attendees: Maya P., Diego A., Priya S., Ethan K., Samira C., Tyler (SRE), Noor (Serving-runtime lead)
Location: #observability-sync Slack huddle + Zoom

Goal for this session:
- Triage two active tracing incidents affecting dashboard accuracy and 1.8x trace storage cost delta observed last month
- Review recent dashboard changes and confirm rollout plan for new cost-attribution panels
- Assign owners for sampling/aggregation experiments to reduce span cardinality

Quick status snapshot (one-liners from standup):
- Maya: finished proof-of-concept for span-family dedupe filter; needs perf run data (next 48h).
- Diego: dashboard query refactor merged to staging; noticed 12% slower load for high-cardinality queries.
- Priya: cost attribution prototype (per-route token mapping) is 60% complete; waiting on PR feedback.
- Ethan: tracing agent bump rolled out to private deploy customers (canary) — no errors; CPU delta +3%.
- Samira: tracing retention policy update doc drafted for legal review.

Notes from triage (incident: traces missing parent-child links in ~2% of requests):
- Symptom: spans from backend-gateway service occasionally arrive with missing parent_id, resulting in orphaned root-level spans that break waterfall views. Affects traces created between 2026-03-28 and 2026-04-01 mostly in us-west-2 region.
- Evidence: correlation between gateway v1.3.7 -> v1.4.0 rollout and spike in orphan spans (see OBS-421).
- Hypothesis 1: instrumentation library change in v1.4.0 that switches to transient trace_id generation when header parsing fails (edge-case with malformed trace parent header).
- Hypothesis 2: concurrent request batching at the gateway occasionally reuses a span context incorrectly when KV cache warmup overlaps with a connection retry.
- Data collected: sample traces (30) saved to /linked_artifacts/OBS-421-samples (attached in Jira).
- Short-term mitigation: detect orphaned spans on ingest and attempt header reassembly using request fingerprint (implemented as hotfix rule in ingestion pipeline, low risk).
- Long-term fix: roll-forward instrumentation patch + add a strict header-validation check in gateway.
- Action: Diego + Ethan to verify hotfix rule performance in staging by 2026-04-04. If rule reduces orphan rate to <0.2%, keep and schedule instrumentation roll-forward.

Tracing / sampling experiments (goal: reduce traces stored by 35% without losing coverage on error paths):
- Maya presented span-family dedupe filter: strategy is to collapse low-value repetitive spans within a trace (e.g., internal cache-check x10 -> keep one representative) before indexing.
  - Expected impact: 20–40% reduction in indexed span count for high-throughput endpoints.
  - Risk: possible loss of debugging fidelity for micro-flaky behaviors; mitigations: keep full verbose trace on error signals and maintain a 1% full-sample stream.
  - Next step: run perf/job to measure indexing throughput and query latency with dedupe enabled (Maya to run and share results 2026-04-04).
- Priya running adaptive sampling prototype: sample rate driven by low-latency threshold and error rate; dynamic windows per service.
  - Integration plan: start on internal services, iterate on thresholds, add to roadmap for Dedicated customers as policy knob.

Dashboards and query optimizations:
- Diego: dashboard query refactor aims to move heavy grouping into pre-aggregated materialized views (MV) to speed up front-end load. Staging results: 2x faster on 90th percentile but 12% slower on one high-cardinality filter.
  - Plan: add a targeted index for that filter and adjust MV refresh cadence to avoid hotspots.
  - Rollout: merge->canary->global over 6 business days. Diego to prepare rollback plan and a flag to switch to legacy view.
- UX tweak: Samira proposed a lightweight "cost per route" column on the traces table so SREs can triage costly endpoints quickly. Agreement: add to next dashboard sprint.

Cost telemetry update (notes from Priya):
- Observed: March invoice shows +1.8x growth in trace storage cost for prod over baseline; top 3 contributors: chat-router, gateway, embedding-service (combined 68% of delta).
- Attribution approach: map ingestion batches to an origin route tag at collection time (token-count × model × route). Early prototype attributes 82% of cost to routes; remaining 18% currently unclassified due to legacy agents.
- Proposed small wins: (1) per-route retention policy (keep longer for high value product flows), (2) dynamic TTL for low-value traces, (3) per-customer quota enforcement for private deployments.
- Action: Priya to land PR for per-route token accounting by 2026-04-06 (PR: linked_artifacts / GitHub PR 274).

Operational decisions and agreements:
- Adopt hotfix ingestion rule for orphan spans (canary ASAP). Owner: Ethan. Target: reduce orphan rate to <0.2%.
- Approve continued work on span-family dedupe filter as opt-in feature for Dedicated customers. Owner: Maya. Deadline: perf numbers by 2026-04-04.
- Begin pre-aggregation MV rollout for dashboards but add targeted index and one-week canary. Owner: Diego. Rollout window: 6 business days after staging sign-off.
- Cost telemetry: land per-route token accounting prototype to staging and run 7-day backfill to validate attributions before enabling alerts. Owner: Priya.

Action items (flat list):
- Ethan: deploy hotfix ingest rule to staging and run 48h validation (2026-04-04).
- Diego: create targeted index and update MV refresh cadence, prepare rollback flag for dashboard refactor (2026-04-06).
- Maya: perf-run span-family dedupe on staging dataset + collect query latency impact (2026-04-04).
- Priya: finish per-route token accounting PR and start 7-day backfill in staging (2026-04-06).
- Samira: finalize retention policy doc and send to Legal for review (2026-04-05).
- Tyler (SRE): add alert for orphan-span-rate crossing 0.5% and instrument dashboard tile (2026-04-07).

Risks / open questions:
- How do we guarantee debugging fidelity if dedupe collapses spans that occasionally carry a unique error signal? (Mitigation: full-sample stream + error-triggered retention.)
- Private customers using older agents will create an attribution gap; do we enforce upgrades or accept partial attribution? (Discuss on next week roadmap).
- Cost vs latency trade-offs for more aggressive pre-aggregation — need SLO review with Product/Console team.

Quick decisions for Product/Console sync:
- We will add a per-route cost card to the Redwood Console alpha dashboard and gate it behind a feature flag. Product action: brief PM on Console to align on rollout and UI copy (Maya to draft).

Misc notes / snippets from discussion:
- "If we can catch 40% of the noisy spans with dedupe, we can buy ~3 months of runway on the existing storage budget." — Diego
- "Keep default sampling conservative for Hosted API; enable experimental knobs for Dedicated customers only." — Noor

Summary / next meeting:
- Next triage sync: 2026-04-06 09:30 PT (short 30-minute checkpoint) to review hotfix results and dedupe perf numbers.
- Next full weekly deep-dive: 2026-04-09 09:30 PT.

Attachments/References:
- Sample orphan traces attached to JIRA OBS-421
- Dashboard query diff: GitHub PR 274
- Retention policy draft: Confluence page

End of notes.
